neighbours.label: The 'all' in a convergence claim that contrasts diversity with one shared outcome ('there are many X, but they all lead to Y'), vs the same diversity setup continued without convergence
fire: Every chef has a different recipe for this stew, but they all start with onions.
The rivers rise in different valleys, but they all flow into the same lake.
My friends have very different jobs, but they all complain about their bosses.
These phone apps look different, but they all collect your location.
The old maps disagree on many details, but they all show the island in the north.
The candidates gave very different speeches, but they all promised lower taxes.
There are dozens of trails in the park, but they all end at the waterfall.
The children chose different instruments, but they all practise in the same room.
quiet: Every chef has a different recipe for this stew, and some are quite spicy.
The rivers rise in different valleys, and each one has its own fish.
My friends have very different jobs, and one of them works at night.
These phone apps look different, and a few of them cost money.
The old maps disagree on many details, especially about the coastline.
The candidates gave very different speeches, and the debate ran late.
There are dozens of trails in the park, and the longest takes a day.
The children chose different instruments, so the concert was noisy.

predictions: '..., but they all <verb>' after a variety setup 0.4-0.8; same setups continued with 'and some of them' or 'but each' under 0.15.
notes: Card: peaks on ' all', ' but', ' they', ' lead', 'ultimately'; the + pole suppresses ' all', ' ultimately', ' everyone', so the - pole sits where a unifying 'all/ultimately' claim is coming. Probe: 'many paths ... but they all lead to the same summit' 0.824 on ' all', 'but ultimately they all come down to' 0.455, 'All roads eventually lead to' 0.234; 'but they are all rooted' only 0.096, 'and some of them are steep' 0.124, 'and some of them are strict' 0.043. Fire items use 'but they all' + verb.
